selection_rationale: cnsms2026-001 (GVR+Batfish) best matches the programme gap (end-to-end generate–verify–repair for NetOps), has strong venue relevance and falsifiability, and is experimentally feasible given public verifiers and datasets once the reviewer-identified weaknesses are repaired.
unresolved_uncertainties: Does verifier-assisted GVR materially reduce real-world outage risk at production scale (external validity) (Q01).
What are empirical trade-offs between verifier coverage/strictness and end-to-end throughput/latency in realistic high-throughput settings (Q02).
How well do constrained/repair approaches prevent semantic violations across diverse, vendor-specific CLIs given incomplete grammar coverage and tokenization differences (Q03).
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify and validate an external oracle or multi-verifier strategy (e.g., Batfish plus secondary checks) to estimate verifier false negatives and report verifier coverage/limitations.
Define precise dataset construction rules, vendor-coverage statistics, and publish the task set, topology suites, and CLI artifacts used (provenance for vendor constructs).
Preregister numeric latency and iteration budgets and operational thresholds (e.g., max median latency, max repair iterations) with justification.
Add prompt-robustness and sensitivity analyses: freeze and publish exact prompts, seeds, LLM model identifier(s), and include prompt-perturbation tests.
Publish CLI grammar/transform artifacts and any syntax parsers used for failure-mode classification; define fallback behavior for incomplete grammars.
Define repair-loop design in detail (LLM prompting for repair, stopping rules, oscillation-detection) and preregister retry budget, deterministic replay procedures, and logging/hash policies.
